doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Editors and the decline of life-story features
summary: Editors once ran long as-told-to stories, but now want current players; Vacher laments no outlet for a Joe Wilder piece.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Do you have to balance what you want to write about and what an editor might want you to write about?

I do now. Much more now. We’re very fortunate. In the 60s when I was getting into my stride on all this, Jazz Monthly, Jazz Journal was also at its peak then. I was writing for Coda in Canada. They almost, there was an openness. I don’t remember any editor saying, “Oh I don’t think we want to publish his story.” That is not the position now. I mean for instance I interviewed John Hicks, a terrific piano player about eighteen months

ago — a couple of years ago. I can not place the full story, an as-told-to oral history type piece on John Hicks. Whereas previously I would prepare someone’s life story, an as- told-to, a literally a sort of let’s start at the beginning and right through to where we are now, and I would place those with magazines like Jazz Journal or Jazz Monthly without question. It might run to five thousand words and no one would be bothered, because that’s something that hadn’t been done and it was something that people wanted to do. I can’t do that now. There just isn’t — well we’ve lost something, certainly in the media I work for, we’ve lost something in the sense of the history of the music. It’s much more about now.
They want to hear more about the now players, the up and comers?

The now players, the players with ahem record company linkages if you’ll understand me. The guys who are pushing the envelope. I’m interested in those people for sure, but I actually think that Joe Wilder’s got the important story. All I can tell you is I’ve just interviewed Joe Wilder up to a point, not very far into his career, and he’s given me a lot of fascinating stuff. There won’t be an English magazine that will want to take a piece on Joe Wilder, which is a shame, isn’t it?
